defects.justification: Gem 'puma' has no version constraint, so bundle install resolves whatever release is newest, including future major versions with breaking changes.
require 'csv' is used but csv is not in the Gemfile; since Ruby 3.4 csv is a bundled (not default) gem, so under bundle exec the require fails on supported Rubies (README says 3.1+).
CsvImport::App.run! on Sinatra ~> 4.0 needs the 'rackup' gem, which is not declared, so the README's 'ruby app.rb' cannot start a server.

POST /imports (and GET /imports/:id) need no authentication, so anyone who can reach the service can upsert/overwrite any customer record by email and read import error messages containing customer data.
The uploaded file is copied to the uploads dir with no size limit (acknowledged in README), so a single request can fill disk.
read_rows collects every parsed CSV row into an array before processing, so memory grows with the (unbounded) upload size.
Every upload spawns a new Thread with no pool or limit, so a burst of uploads creates unbounded concurrent imports competing for the SQLite write lock and memory.
JOBS[id] stores a Thread object for every import ever started and nothing ever removes entries, so the hash grows for the life of the process.
Each upload is copied to uploads/<id>.csv and the file is never deleted after the import finishes, so disk usage grows without bound.
CSV.open is called without a 'bom|utf-8' encoding, so a CSV saved by Excel with a UTF-8 BOM gets a header '\uFEFFname' and the whole import fails with 'missing columns: name'.
